title: Lecture 3 – MSK pathology
html:
Source: Curs 3 engleza.pptx – 176 slides

Agent : #1

  • Staphylococcus aureus (75 %)
  • Streptococci; other germs
  • Contamination:
  • Hematogenous – most common
  • Direct seeding: accidental / iatrogenous
  • Contiguity
  • Affecting: any age, more frequent in children, M/F = 3/1
  • Osteomyelitis

Pathophysiology #2

  • Affects highly vascular bone
  • Metaphysis in children
  • Vertebrae in adults
  • Usually involves a single bone, single place
  • Can become chronic, evolution in bursts

X-ray: #3

  • Can be normal
  • Changes appear gradually
  • Osteoporosis, then osteolysis
  • Periosteal reaction
  • Osteomyelitis: early stage

US: #4

  • Soft tissue edema
  • Subperiosteal abscess
  • Osteomyelitis: early stage

MRI: #5

  • Best diagnostic tool
  • Early detection of bone marrow edema:
  • T1 hypointense
  • T2 hyperintense
  • Contrast enhancement
  • Abscess
  • Osteomyelitis: early stage

Notes: A: Coronal T1-weighted image of the right knee of a 4-year-old male shows ill-defined areas of low T1 signal in the bone marrow in the lateral femoral metaphysis (arrow) and lateral epiphysis (arrowhead); B: Coronal T1-weighted post-contrast image in the same patient shows associated enhancement in these areas (white arrow and arrowhead) as well as some periosteal reaction, indicated by periosteal enhancement (black arrow). Pugmire BS, Shailam R, Gee MS. Role of MRI in the diagnosis and treatment of osteomyelitis in pediatric patients. World J Radiol 2014; 6(8): 530-537 [PMID: 25170391 DOI: 10.4329/wjr.v6.i8.530]

MRI: #6

  • Best diagnostic tool
  • Early detection of bone marrow edema:
  • T1 hypointense
  • T2 hyperintense
  • Contrast enhancement
  • Abscess
  • Osteomyelitis: early stage

Notes: Sagittal T2-weighted image with fat suppression shows a large subperiosteal abscess (solid arrow) with adjacent soft tissue edema (arrowhead); Pugmire BS, Shailam R, Gee MS. Role of MRI in the diagnosis and treatment of osteomyelitis in pediatric patients. World J Radiol 2014; 6(8): 530-537 [PMID: 25170391 DOI: 10.4329/wjr.v6.i8.530]

Osteomyelitis #7

X-ray, CT, MRI: #8

  • Cloaca (lytic cavity)
  • Sequestrum (sclerotic devascularized bone inside the cloaca)
  • Draining sinus
  • Involucrum (sclerotic rim delineating the lesions)
  • Osteomyelitis: acute-chronic stage

X-ray, CT, MRI: #9

  • Lytic cavity (filled with pus)
  • Sequestrum (sclerotic devascularized bone inside the lytic cavity)
  • Cloaca (drainage orifice)
  • Involucrum (sclerotic rim delineating the lesions usually by periosteal apposition)
  • Osteomyelitis: acute->chronic stage

X-ray, CT, MRI: #10

  • Lytic cavity (filled with pus)
  • Sequestrum (sclerotic devascularized bone inside the lytic cavity)
  • Cloaca (drainage orifice)
  • Involucrum (sclerotic rim delineating the lytic cavity usually by periosteal apposition)
  • Osteomyelitis: acute->chronic stage

Osteomyelitis - chronic #11

CT: #12

  • sequestration
  • Cortical thickening
  • Fistulae - fistulography
  • Soft tissue abscess (± contrast)
  • Osteomyelitis - chronic
  • MRI:
  • Active foci
  • abscess
  • fibrosis
  • sequestration
  • Soft tissue abscess

Bone whitlow #13

  • Soft tissue swelling
  • Surface osteolysis
  • NO periostosis
  • Osteomyelitis

Osteomyelitis: complications #14

  • Complication
  • Septic arthritis
  • Pathologic fracture
  • Pathologic fracture healing
  • Limb deformity
  • (shortening / lengthening)

Septic arthritis #15

  • Agent: most commonly
  • Staphylococcus aureus
  • Seeding:
  • hematogenous
  • direct
  • contiguity
  • Age groups:
  • Children <3 y.o.
  • Teenagers
  • Elderly
  • Comorbidities/immunosuppresion

Septic arthritis #16

  • Location:
  • Any joint
  • More frequent:
  • Hip in kids
  • Knee in adults
  • Sacroiliac or sternoclavicular joints in diabetes, HIV, drug abuse.

  • X-ray
  • Often normal
  • Periarticular osteoporosis sometimes seen

Notes: (A) Initial normal left hip radiograph. (B) Subtle joint space narrowing (arrow). (C) Complete loss of joint space (arrow). (D) Joint destruction with flattening of the femoral head (arrow). (E) Left hip excision arthroplasty with a temporary spacer. (F) Total hip replacement after 12 weeks of intravenous antibiotics, normal inflammatory markers and a negative hip aspirate.

Ankylosis #26

  • Disappearance of the joint space
  • Bone fusion across a joint
  • ONLY produced by arthritis
  • NEVER produced by arthrosis

  • Same as RX

Septic arthritis- MRI #29

  • Within 24 hrs from onset
  • T1:
  • Subchondral hyposignal on both bones
  • Fluid sensitive sequences:
  • Hypersignal: fluid in joint, surrounding edema .
  • Postcontrast:
  • Synovial enhancement
  • Subchondral enhancement
  • ± soft tissue abscess

Septic arthritis- US #30

  • Small fluid effusions
  • Thickened syovial membrane + Doppler signal in acute phase
  • US guided joint punctures
  • diagnostic

Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) #31

  • Definition
  • = chronic inflammatory disease primary involving the small joints of the extremities
  • Caused by an autoimmune reaction mainly involving the synovium
  • Incidence
  • 1% population
  • F : M = 3 : 1

RA: location #32

  • Symmetrical (± unilateral in early stages)
  • Joints involved:
  • Hands (most commonly)
  • Metacarpophalangeal 85%
  • Carpal 80%
  • Proximal interphalangeal 75%
  • Distal interphalangeal almost never involved !!!
  • Feet
  • Other joints: cervical spine, knee, elbow…

  • Bilateral swelling MCPh, PIPh, MTF, NOT DIPh
  • Subcutaneous rheumatoid nodules
  • Typical RX changes,
  • Positive rheumatoid factor
  • Pathology – rheumatoid nodule

Ankylosing spondilytis (AS) #58

  • definition
  • Inflammatory arthropathy & enthesopathy mainly affecting the axial skeleton

Clinic #59

  • Persistent, progressive
  • Nocturnal
  • Bilateral
  • Sensitivity on local pressure
  • Objective signs
  • Occipital – wall dist.
  • Finger – ground dist.
  • Schober Test
  • Chest expansion
  • late
  • Wolf neck
  • Skier position
  • stepping

Gout #84

  • Epidemiology:
  • < 5 % of hyperuricemia pts; 5% of arthritis pts.;
  • Age:
  • 30 – 60 yrs
  • M : F = 20 : 1
  • Hyperuricemia → uric acid deposits in soft tissues, cartilage, bone → inflammation, destruction
  • Predisposing factors:
  • Metabolic sdr.: obesity, HBP, Diabetes, endstage renal disease, alcohol, diuretics…

Gout – clinical data #85

  • characteristics:
  • Hyperuricemia → uric acid deposits in soft tissues, cartilage, bone → inflammation, destruction
  • Primary: acute attack
  • Chronic: gouty tophi
  • Idiopathic, familial
  • Sinovial!

Gout #86

  • Location:
  • Any location!!
  • Oligo-, but may be polyarticular, asymmetric
  • Most commonly:
  • MTPh I
  • Lower extremities. > sup.
  • Small joints > large

Osteoarthritis (Arthrosis) #96

  • Definition: degenerative joint disease due to the breakdown of the cartilage and of the subchondral bone
  • The most frequent arthropathy (1 in 7 adults)
  • Caused by:
  • Mechanical stress on the joint
  • Low grade inflammatory process
  • Risk factors:
  • Age
  • Obesity
  • Trauma
  • Genetics (significant family history)
  • Etc…

Osteoarthritis #97

  • ARTHROSIS NEVER PRODUCES BONE ANKYLOSIS !!!

  • Osteophytes

  • Triangle, wide base attached to bone, tip distally
  • Covered by cartilage invisible on X-ray
  • May form bridges
